newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican lawyer detained over suspected bomb links.
newsitem.headline: Corsican lawyer detained over suspected bomb links.

text.p: Police detained a lawyer, who is also a close friend of fugitive Corsican separatist leader Francois Santoni, on Monday over suspected links to a bomb attack on a golf club, police sources said.

The detention of lawyer Marie-Helene Mattei brought to nine the number of suspects in custody in connection with Thursday's attack on the Sperone golf course, which investigators believe was linked to an extortion racket run by Corsican separatists.

Investigators said Mattei's arrest was a sign of the government's determination to restore order on the holiday Mediterranean island after President Jacques Chirac last week said bombers would be tracked down relentlessly.

Mattei is the lawyer of Cuncolta Naziunalista, the legal wing of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) which last week threatened to step up attacks on the French mainland as part of its drive for more autonomy from Paris.
She is also a close friend of Cuncolta leader Santoni who has been in hiding to avoid weapons charges, though he appeared in a television interview on Friday, urging talks with Chirac.

Thursday's bomb flattened the golf course keeper's house but caused no injuries. The FLNC claimed responsibility for the bombing, accusing the golf course owners of letting French commandos use the building.
The owners filed a legal complaint, saying they had been asked for money in a mafia-style, cash-for-protection racket.

No-one had filed such a complaint before, and investigators are hoping the case could prove a watershed in a battle against a widely-rumoured "revolutionary tax" levied by guerrillas on hotel and restaurant owners.
The FLNC said in a statement last week it planned "new forms" of attacks on the mainland in its two-decade-old campaign to win greater autonomy for the island.
